Existing OpenFGA identity/workflow/view relations and human organization/environment roles can support an explicitly reviewed new operation without inventing principals. Existing relations do not themselves authorize an unregistered operation or prove physical routing.

recommended_next_connected_design.product_flow: Explicit administrative admission of an existing typed Agent to an existing active native Device and exact current credential generation, plus native Device acceptance. Label as admitted association; expose provenance/freshness/revocation. This is configuration testimony, not observed routing or enforcement.
recommended_next_connected_design.identity: Reuse original scoped Agent ID and selected admitted source-native identity and original native Device ID/credential/generation. Do not create an identity kind, FGA principal, provider credential, inventory Device alias or auto-grant.
recommended_next_connected_design.permission_boundary: Keep two alternatives distinct: (A) NEW closed operation using existing manage_identity on Agent/environment, requiring explicit new operation/multi-target proof admission; (B) explicit versioned updateAgent actions with original manage_workflows on the single Agent, current original human identity/PAT ceilings and separately signed native Device consent. Neither alternative is admitted or implemented by this audit. Do not infer public Device management authority, widen legacy owner/team/tags input, add a Device source kind or alter global updateAgent FreshAuth=false. Root/independent finite design must select exact authority and risk semantics before product changes.
two_sided_admission_candidate: Phase1: a new current Agent-authorized operation (versioned updateAgent candidate or explicitly admitted new operation) creates a bounded expiring idempotent challenge for the existing scoped Agent/source identity, operator-intended existing Device ID, exact nonce/intent digest, author and audit provenance. Supplied Device ID is an expectation, not identity authority or permission to enumerate/manage Devices. No active association is created.

Phase2: the intentional operator uses the already enrolled Device current local credential to sign the exact challenge acceptance via existing native HTTP proof. Native server derives actual scope/Device/credential/generation/expiry from current authority, verifies exact intended Device/challenge/nonce and persists pending acceptance. Device alone cannot activate an Agent association.

Phase3: a separate new current Agent-authorized confirmation under the selected finite contract revalidates original human identity/membership/PAT ceilings/current OpenFGA permission and exact Agent/source, verifies original author/intent/nonce and current same-generation Device acceptance/expiry after waits, and activates only after confirmed commit. A phase1 authorization80 context is transaction-bound and cannot delegate human authority across phases; original human revocation prevents phase3.
recommended_next_connected_design.persistence: If an additive profile is required, one finite application profile for the connected admission/acceptance/finalize/read/revoke flow, not a profile per phase. Reuse original registered discovery source authority and exact original API/native gateway callers with minimal reviewed function grants, FORCE RLS/seals and existing lock ordering. Existing exact ownership-write profile is not widened or reused for arbitrary association SQL. No immutable source/profile/grant rewrite.
recommended_next_connected_design.source_freshness: Bind the immutable scoped source-native Agent identity and provenance source, record exact admission snapshot/evidence. Current reads must revalidate active/fresh source identity. Freeze whether subsequent same-identity last-good snapshots retain the association rather than invalidating every normal sync; changed UID/source identity never auto-rebinds. Annotation owner/team/tag changes do not authenticate routing.
recommended_next_connected_design.revocation: Explicit association revoke/CAS and source removal/tombstone/freshness loss, Device revoke/delete, credential expiry/rotation and wrong scope must make association unavailable. Old generation cannot silently transfer. Current user permission/session revocation denies new intent/finalization/read immediately via original current authorization. Decide separately whether completed administrative configuration persists after its historical author loses permissions; it must never grant that author ongoing access.
recommended_next_connected_design.multiplicity: Freeze many-Agent-per-Device and multi-Device-per-Agent semantics explicitly. No inferred exclusive, all-instance or fleet claim. Every selected source/device/generation relation needs bounded independent evidence.
recommended_next_connected_design.read_ui: One connected Agent-detail operator flow: current API creates challenge, explicit existing Device credential signs acceptance, browser/operator confirms under a new current Agent request, actual typed read shows admitted/pending/revoked/source-stale/device-unavailable/credential-rotated evidence, and authorized revoke works. No Device key or enrollment secret enters the browser or arbitrary public proof body; no covered/healthy filter is emitted.
recommended_next_connected_design.scope_limit: Administrative admission plus Device possession does not prove that the Agent workload actually uses that Device. Actual routing/workload identity proof remains a separate required design if the original coverage requirement depends on observed enforcement. No local event attribute, IP, namespace, pod colocation, mutable annotation or policy GET can substitute.

human_freshness_source_research.existing_operation: updateAgent registry currently FreshAuth=false and supports BrowserSession/ProductAPIToken under manage_workflows. Its current ownership SQL require_api explicitly expects fresh_auth=false in the transaction proof.
human_freshness_source_research.existing_identity: Current browser authentication independently loads FreshAuthenticated and FreshAuthExpiresAt from actual session authenticated_at within five minutes, current session revocation/expiry, active membership and effective scope. PAT authentication supplies owning human and current permission ceiling; it does not have recent browser authentication.
human_freshness_source_research.existing_router: Router freshAuthenticated accepts a bearer token or a recent browser session when an operation requires fresh auth. Therefore setting a global fresh flag alone does not imply browser-only step-up.
human_freshness_source_research.existing_sql: authorization80 identity_fence checks actual current credential/session/membership; its five-minute authenticated_at check is conditional on request proof fresh_auth. A phase1 context cannot remain a transferable human authorization because current SQL context and grant seals are transaction-bound.
human_freshness_source_research.unresolved: Choose explicitly between new current request revalidation and mandatory recent browser/Stytch authentication for association intent/finalize. If step-up is required on a selected version of updateAgent, both handler and SQL/native current-credential checks and request-proof admission must agree without globally changing the legacy operation or pretending PAT is a fresh browser session. This is a real security contract choice, not a completed check.
